The current check only handles the case where the environment variable is explicitly `undefined`. If `MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST` is an empty string (common in some deployment environments) or a non-numeric string, `Number()` will return `0` or `NaN` respectively. Since the Zod schema in `validators.ts` has a `.min(1)` constraint and `z.number()` rejects `NaN`, the application will still throw a validation error on startup. To ensure the 'graceful degradation' and 'NaN-safe' behavior mentioned in the PR description, consider a more robust check that falls back to `undefined` for any non-numeric or empty input.

```suggestion
maxImagesPerRequest: (env.MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST && !isNaN(Number(env.MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST))) ? Number(env.MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST) : undefined,
```

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep JSON error bodies for non-2xx responses**

This early throw turns every non-2xx API result into a transport error and prevents callers from reading contract-shaped error payloads. In this repo, UI flows call `postJson(...)` and then parse `payload` to surface specific server messages/codes; after this change, valid JSON errors (for example 400/502 responses from `/api/generate` or `/api/tools`) are replaced by a generic `postJson: HTTP ...` message from `catch`, which regresses user-visible diagnostics and removes actionable error context.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve downstream image-generation error semantics**

This guard collapses all non-2xx responses from `/api/image-generation` into a synthetic `IMAGE_HTTP_ERROR` with status 502, discarding the original status and contract error body. `runImageGenerationPipeline` emits meaningful error codes/statuses (including 400 and 503 cases), and this change prevents `/api/generate` from propagating those distinctions, which can misclassify failures and hide root cause details needed by clients and operators.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

`postJson` now throws immediately when `!response.ok`, which prevents callers from reading the JSON `{ ok: false, error: ... }` payload that the API routes return on 4xx/5xx (e.g. `/api/generate`, `/api/tools` return `json(pipelineResult.body, { status: pipelineResult.status })`). This is a behavioral change that will cause UI code to fall back to the generic thrown error message instead of displaying the server-provided error message/details. Consider still parsing and returning the payload even for non-2xx responses (or throwing a richer error that includes the parsed payload) so consumers can surface contract errors consistently.

This branch treats a non-2xx HTTP response as `IMAGE_NETWORK_ERROR`, but the message indicates an HTTP status code. That makes it harder to distinguish true network/transport failures (fetch throws) from upstream HTTP errors; consider using an `IMAGE_HTTP_ERROR` code (and optionally include the status in `details`) for the `!response.ok` case.

When returning `IMAGE_HTTP_ERROR` for a non-ok image-generation response, consider including the upstream status code in `details` (e.g. `{ status: String(imageResponse.status) }`) to keep the status machine-readable and consistent with other HTTP error shapes in the codebase.

This change adds a new behavior where an absent `MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST` env var becomes `undefined` and relies on the Zod `.default(4)` to fill it in. There’s unit coverage for AppConfigSeam parsing, but no test currently asserts the new defaulting behavior when `MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST` is missing; adding one would prevent regressions (e.g. reverting to `NaN` again).

**issue (bug_risk):** Guard against NaN when parsing MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST from the environment.

If `MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST` is non-numeric, `Number(...)` returns `NaN`, which Zod will likely reject, causing an unclear startup failure. Either coerce non-finite values to `undefined` (e.g., via `Number.isFinite(parsed)`) so the schema default applies, or explicitly throw a clearer configuration error when the env var is invalid.

✅ Addressed in dc835d328b570741ca4d1e7423a65cde61d96809: `maxImagesPerRequest` now checks for a defined, numeric `MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST` value and falls back to `undefined` when parsing fails, preventing NaN from reaching the Zod schema.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve upstream status for non-JSON image failures**

When `/api/image-generation` returns a non-2xx response with a non-JSON body (for example an HTML 503 from a proxy), this branch always maps the pipeline response status to `502` instead of propagating `imageResponse.status`, so callers lose the original failure class (e.g., 429 vs 503) and may apply the wrong retry/user messaging behavior. Fresh evidence: the new non-JSON edge-case test uses a 503 upstream response, and this code path still hardcodes a 502 pipeline status.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject malformed MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST values**

This coercion now treats any non-numeric `MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST` string as if the variable were unset and silently falls back to the schema default of `4`, which hides real configuration mistakes (for example `MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST=abc`) that previously failed fast during startup. That makes bad production config look healthy while applying an unintended limit, which is especially hard to detect during deploys.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
